finding.title: Sync push payloads embed client-clock timestamps as the cross-device LWW ordering field instead of FieldValue.serverTimestamp()

evidence.quote:
the device with the
strictly newer timestamp wins.
// remote document carries a valid LWW timestamp. The merger

finding.why: docs/sync-conflict-resolution.md's own Push/pull invariant says the device with the 'strictly newer timestamp' wins LWW races. Every updated_at value this batch's push payloads carry comes from `_clock.nowUtc()` (LocalDayClock, ultimately the device's own system clock) or a Drift-stored value stamped by the device clock at write time -- never FieldValue.serverTimestamp(). coding-standards.md's own FB-2 rationale names the exact failure: 'two devices with skewed clocks writing client timestamps make last-write-wins non-deterministic -- the faster clock always wins and silently overwrites newer data.' A device with a wrong/stuck system clock (common on hand-me-down or long-offline tablets, which this family-learning app explicitly supports offline) will have every goals/curriculum_tracks/settings/gamification_settings push either always lose or always win LWW races regardless of actual edit recency, silently discarding another device's real edits with no error surfaced anywhere.
finding.recommendation: Route the LWW ordering field for mutable-document pushes through FieldValue.serverTimestamp() at the Firestore-gateway layer (the codebase already does this correctly for the separate synced_at field in firestore_gateway_impl.dart), keeping the client timestamp only as a local optimistic-ordering hint per FB-2's own wording. The fix site is core/sync/ (gateway + merge layer), outside this batch; these two files are the clearest evidence, not the fix location.
acceptance_criteria: FB-2 Rule-0 checker per coding-standards.md: audit grep asserting no DateTime.now()-derived value feeds a sync codec's ordering field, plus an emulator test asserting the persisted ordering field is a server Timestamp.
Extend test/integration/two_device_sync_test.dart (or add a sibling test) with a case that sets one device's local clock backward and asserts its genuinely later edit still wins the LWW race.
